# Node.js 20.9.0 (LTS)

[RL](https://github.com/richardlau)

Richard Lau

Node.js 20.9.0 (LTS)

## [2023-10-24, Version 20.9.0 'Iron' (LTS), @richardlau](#2023-10-24-version-2090-iron-lts-richardlau)

### [Notable Changes](#notable-changes)

This release marks the transition of Node.js 20.x into Long Term Support (LTS) with the codename 'Iron'.

The 20.x release line now moves into "Active LTS" and will remain so until October 2024.

After that time, it will move into "Maintenance" until end of life in April 2026.

### [Known issue](#known-issue)

Collecting code coverage via the `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` environment variable may lead to a hang.

This is not thought to be a regression in Node.js 20 (some reports are on Node.js 18).

For more information, including some potential workarounds, see issue [#49344](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/49344).

Quick Answer

How much does ChatGPT cost?

ChatGPT pricing spans six plans: Free at $0, Go at $8/month, Plus at $20/month, Pro at $100 or $200/month depending on usage tier, Business at $20/seat/month billed annually ($25 monthly, two-seat minimum), and Enterprise at custom pricing.

Paid tiers add the newest GPT-5.6 models, higher limits, and tools like Deep Research and Agent mode.

OpenAI now sells ChatGPT six different ways, and three of the tiers cost within a few dollars of each other per person.

Picking wrong is easy, and it happens in both directions: individuals paying $200 for usage they’d never hit, and teams handling client data on $20 Plus accounts that lack the one guarantee they legally need.

The plan cards don’t make the differences obvious.
